NONE is temporal, and temporal transfer is the axis that matters most for a deployment recommendation: a site deciding whether to federate is applying a rule fitted on historical data. Freddie Mac 2017 is a different origination year -- 1.38M loans, the same 16-feature schema, the same 0.035 default rate, and the same four partitions -- so it is a clean held-out year rather than a new collection. PREDICTION: the adequacy gradient replicates in sign and rough magnitude on 2017, and the ordering of partitions by mean benefit is preserved against the original year. FALSIFIABLE AND IMPORTANT EITHER WAY: if the gradient or the ordering does not survive a change of year on the same lender, the same schema and the same outcome, then every cross-collection replication in the paper is weaker than it looks -- because a rule that cannot cross a year boundary on identical data has no business crossing a domain boundary. WITHDRAWAL CONDITION: if the sign of rho(EPV, benefit) flips between years on the same partition, section 4 must report temporal instability as a limitation rather than claim replication.
